29 Which diagram shows the electric field pattern of an isolated negative point charge?
D
A
B
C
–
–
–
–

hints: Notice whether the field lines in A and B are straight radial lines or closed circles centred on the $- $ charge.
Recall that electric field direction is the direction of the force on a small positive test charge placed in the field.
Compare diagrams C and D: both are radial, but only one has all arrows pointing toward the negative charge that attracts a positive test charge.
walkthrough: Identify the source: a single isolated negative point charge marked $- $ at the centre, so the field must be symmetric in all directions.
State the rule for shape: the field of an isolated point charge is radial, with straight field lines meeting the charge at right angles, not closed circular loops.
This eliminates A and B, which show concentric circles like a magnetic field pattern.
State the rule for direction: field direction is the force on a positive test charge, so a negative source charge attracts it and all arrows must point inward toward the centre.
Diagram C shows radial lines pointing outward, away from the charge, while diagram D shows radial lines pointing inward, toward the charge. This is option D.

A.explanation: Circular loops around the charge are not produced by a static point charge - they suggest a magnetic field, not a radial electric field.

B.explanation: Circular loops in the opposite sense are still not radial, so they cannot represent the electric field of an isolated point charge.

C.explanation: Radial straight lines are correct in shape but the arrows point away from the $- $ charge, which is the pattern for an isolated positive charge.

D.explanation: Straight radial lines with arrows pointing directly toward the $- $ charge show attraction of a positive test charge by a negative charge.
